headline: GOOG surged +6.4% last night and the NASDAQ ripped +6.6% — the biggest single-day tech rally in months — while the ASX closed mildly lower today and Pilbara Minerals popped +4.6% on the local market.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: GOOG had a huge night last night, surging +6.4% as part of a broad tech and AI rally that sent the NASDAQ up 6.6% — the biggest single-day gain in over 18 months for semis and AI stocks. No specific Alphabet news drove it; this was a rising-tide moment for the whole tech sector.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS closed up +4.6% today in a solid session for the lithium miner. No major company-specific news — the bounce likely reflects short-covering and a bit of optimism around lithium demand. The stock remains deeply underwater overall (down ~59% on your cost base), so one day's pop doesn't change the bigger picture.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft climbed +2.4% last night, carried higher by the same broad AI/tech rally that lifted GOOG. Analysts flagged strong earnings momentum but noted the technical setup is still recovering. Up 12% on your cost base overall — solid long-term hold.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE nudged up +0.9% today in a quiet ASX session. Emerging markets have had a rough run this year, and the fund is still down ~8.4% on your cost base. No specific catalyst today — just gentle positive drift.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO was essentially flat last night (+0.01%), which is surprising given the massive GTA 6 launch news — Rockstar reported approximately $3.79 billion in day-one sales with players averaging 8 hours each. The lack of a bigger pop may mean the launch was already priced in, or the market is focused elsewhere.

movers.name: BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF
movers.note: DHHF slipped a tiny -0.17% today, essentially flat in a quiet ASX session. Nothing to worry about — this is normal daily noise for a broadly diversified ETF.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG eased -0.3% today, mirroring the slightly softer ASX. No specific catalyst — the broader market was mildly in the red. Long-term story unchanged for this diversified growth fund.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS closed down -0.64% today on the ASX, but this doesn't reflect last night's massive US rally (+4.9% on the S&P 500) — that gain will flow through to VTS in tomorrow's session. Sit tight, there's a good session likely coming.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI slipped -1.55% today despite the huge AI rally last night on Wall Street. As an ASX-listed ETF, it tracks ASX trading hours and hasn't yet captured last night's massive US semiconductor and AI rebound — expect it to bounce tomorrow when the US gains flow through.

watch_today.title: VTS.AX and GXAI.AX: Expect a bounce tomorrow
watch_today.detail: Both VTS and GXAI closed slightly lower today on the ASX — but they haven't yet priced in last night's monster US rally (S&P +4.9%, NASDAQ +6.6%, semis and AI stocks up sharply). Tomorrow's ASX open should see these two catch up. No action needed — this is good news for long-term holders.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: Same story — big bounce likely tomorrow
watch_today.detail: GXAI fell -1.55% today but the AI/semiconductor ETF (SOXX) had its biggest single-day gain in over 18 months last night in the US. GXAI tracks this space closely. It's still down 22.8% on your cost base, but last night's rally is a real positive for the long-term AI thesis. Hold and let the bounce come through.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 launched — $3.8B day one but stock barely moved
watch_today.detail: Rockstar reported approximately $3.79 billion in GTA 6 day-one sales, with players averaging 8 hours each — a blockbuster launch by any measure. TTWO was flat last night (+0.01%), suggesting the market had largely priced this in. You're down ~2.7% on cost. The long-term thesis (GTA 6 is a multi-year revenue machine) remains intact. No reason to sell — hold and let the game's commercial lifecycle play out.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Nice day but the hole is still deep
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals bounced +4.58% today, which is welcome — but you're still down nearly 60% on your original investment. No fundamental news drove today's move; it looks like a short-term bounce. The lithium market remains depressed. If you believe in the long-term lithium/EV thesis, hold. If this was always a speculative punt, today's pop is worth reflecting on.

watch_today.title: Australian economy warning: Chalmers says 'things will get harder'
watch_today.detail: Treasurer Jim Chalmers warned today that unemployment will surpass 5% and growth will slow further heading into 2027. One indicator watched by economists is flashing recession risk as early as next month. Rate hikes are still possible before any relief in late 2027. This is a headwind for consumer stocks and property — your diversified ETFs (DHHF, VDHG) already have some buffer built in.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Big night — still slightly underwater overall
watch_today.detail: GOOG surged +6.42% last night as part of the broader tech rally. You're still down ~8.6% on cost base in AUD terms (partly due to currency). Nothing has broken the long-term Google/AI story — this looks like the market reasserting tech's value after a soft patch. Hold.

world.summary: Global attention is split between Iran nuclear tensions, the collapse of COP climate talks, a historic tennis milestone, and a major Okinawa cultural moment.

stories.title: Trump wants a 'permanent' Iran nuclear deal — but warns next move may not come until 2027
stories.why_it_matters: Donald Trump has said he wants a 'permanent' deal with Iran over its nuclear program, but indicated the next significant move in negotiations might not happen until 2027. Meanwhile, Iran unveiled a new missile launcher and commanders publicly touted their capabilities. Israeli former senior official Eisenkot said there's no immediate Iranian threat requiring Israeli military action. This diplomatic uncertainty is keeping oil markets jumpy — crude fell sharply last night (down -4.4% to $80.29/barrel) as supply concerns eased, but a flare-up could reverse that quickly.

stories.title: Global climate talks broke down — here's what actually happened
stories.why_it_matters: The latest round of international climate negotiations collapsed without agreement, with wealthy and developing nations failing to bridge the gap on who pays for the energy transition. No article text was available, but the breakdown signals that the global consensus on climate action is under real strain — particularly as the US under Trump has pulled back from climate commitments. For Australian investors, this could mean delays to the global clean energy buildout, which matters for holdings in lithium (PLS) and green-economy ETFs.

stories.title: Carlos Alcaraz wins ATP Finals — joins elite club of Agassi, Federer and Djokovic
stories.why_it_matters: Carlos Alcaraz beat Alexander Zverev in the final of the ATP Finals in Turin, becoming only the fourth player in history to win all four Grand Slams AND the ATP Finals — joining Andre Agassi, Roger Federer, and Novak Djokovic in that exclusive club. At just 23, Alcaraz is cementing himself as potentially the greatest of his generation. Big tennis news heading into the Australian summer season.

stories.title: Okinawa celebrates the return of Shuri Castle's main hall after 36 years
stories.why_it_matters: Okinawa's Shuri Castle — the iconic symbol of Ryukyu Kingdom culture — has officially reopened its main hall, more than three decades after a devastating fire destroyed it in 1992. The restoration is a major cultural milestone for the island and for Japan, with the castle being one of Okinawa's most visited World Heritage sites. It's a rare good-news story in an often turbulent part of the world.

stories.title: Oil drops sharply as Middle East tension eases slightly and global supply rises
stories.why_it_matters: Crude oil (WTI) fell $3.69 or -4.4% last night to $80.29 a barrel, as signals that an immediate Israel-Iran military escalation is unlikely combined with rising global supply to push prices lower. For everyday Australians, this could mean some relief at the petrol pump in coming weeks. For markets, cheaper oil is generally good for airlines and consumer spending, but can weigh on energy stocks.

markets.summary: The US had a blockbuster night last night — the NASDAQ surged +6.6% and the S&P 500 jumped +4.9% in one of the strongest single-session rallies in recent memory, led by AI and semiconductor stocks. Back home, the ASX closed slightly lower today (-0.26%) as the local market waited to see if the US gains would flow through. Oil dropped sharply on easing Middle East tension, and gold surged +4% to a new high of $3,656/oz.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Quiet session today — the ASX missed the US rally as it was already closed. Expect a stronger open tomorrow.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Huge night last night — up nearly 5% in one session, the biggest rally in months, driven by AI and tech stocks.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: The NASDAQ ripped +6.6% last night — semis and AI stocks led the charge in one of the strongest sessions in over 18 months.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil dropped sharply last night as Middle East escalation fears eased and global supply data came in strong. Good news for petrol prices.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold surged +4% to $3,656/oz last night — investors are piling into the safe haven amid geopolitical uncertainty around Iran and stalled climate talks.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar slipped slightly to US$0.663, weighed down by weak domestic economic data and recession talk from Treasurer Chalmers.

politics.summary: A big week for Australian economic anxiety — Treasurer Chalmers warned of rising unemployment and harder times ahead, the RBA flagged potential inflation risks from Labor's tax reform plans, and the government's controversial defence and internet legislation is heading for a Senate showdown.

stories.title: Chalmers warns unemployment will top 5% and 'things will get a bit harder'
stories.why_it_matters: Treasurer Jim Chalmers told Australians today to brace for a tougher year ahead — unemployment is forecast to exceed 5%, growth is slowing, and inflation forecasts have worsened. Chalmers stopped short of calling a recession, but one closely watched economic indicator is reportedly flashing recession risk as early as next month. For everyday Aussies, this means job security could soften and cost-of-living pressures may persist longer than hoped. Mortgage holders face the possibility of further rate hikes before any RBA relief in late 2027.

stories.title: RBA warns Labor's capital gains tax reforms could stoke inflation
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank has modelled Labor's proposed capital gains tax (CGT) reforms — which would reduce the 50% CGT discount investors currently get — and warned the changes could add to inflation. CGT reform means people who sell assets like investment properties or shares pay more tax on the profit. The RBA's concern is that squeezing investors could have unintended knock-on effects for prices. This adds pressure to Labor's reform agenda and could affect property investors and share holders alike.

stories.title: Penny Wong: Australia cannot 'abandon the US' despite Trump turmoil
stories.why_it_matters: Foreign Minister Penny Wong pushed back against Labor critics urging Australia to distance itself from the US under the Trump administration. Wong argued that Australia cannot simply 'abandon' the alliance, even as Trump's tariffs and foreign policy create friction. This comes as Wong also moved to elevate AI as a formal national security and foreign policy challenge — positioning Australia as a country that takes the geopolitical dimensions of artificial intelligence seriously.

stories.title: Labor's defence bill sparks 'war on democracy' accusations
stories.why_it_matters: Labor's new defence legislation, which would allow secret national security rules to be made without public scrutiny, is under fire. A constitutional law expert branded the bill 'lazy and irresponsible,' while civil liberties groups called it a 'war against democracy.' Critics say the laws could allow the government to impose classified obligations on companies and citizens without proper oversight. Supporters say critics are 'jumping at shadows.' The bill is heading for a Senate vote where the Greens are expected to be the deciding vote.

stories.title: Google cancels funding for 25 Australian news outlets
stories.why_it_matters: Google has pulled funding from 25 Australian news outlets, raising fresh concerns about the future of local journalism and the effectiveness of Australia's News Media Bargaining Code. The Code was designed to force tech giants to pay news publishers for using their content, but Google's move suggests it is finding ways around the spirit of those obligations. For media organisations and regional news consumers, this is a significant blow.

ai.summary: AI governance is the dominant theme today — Australia is making it a foreign policy priority, the US Catholic Church is pushing for regulation, and lawyers are being told it's their top challenge. On the product front, China's GLM-5.4 launched and Ant Group open-sourced a medical AI model family.

stories.title: Penny Wong to formally elevate AI as a national security and foreign policy challenge
stories.why_it_matters: Foreign Minister Penny Wong is set to formally name AI as a major foreign policy challenge for Australia — the first time the government has elevated it to this level. The move signals Canberra wants a seat at the table in shaping global AI rules and norms, particularly as competition between the US and China in AI accelerates. For Australian businesses and investors in the AI space, this suggests more government engagement (and potentially more regulation) on the horizon.

stories.title: US Catholic Church launches nationwide push for AI regulation
stories.why_it_matters: The US Catholic Church has launched a coordinated nationwide campaign calling for federal AI regulation, arguing that AI poses ethical risks around human dignity, job displacement, and social justice that the market alone won't solve. The Church is pushing for laws that ensure AI systems are transparent and accountable. It's a notable entry of a major moral institution into the AI policy debate, adding pressure on US legislators who have so far been slow to pass comprehensive AI laws.

stories.title: Washington Post: America's AI policy has a 'chip-size hole' in it
stories.why_it_matters: An opinion piece in the Washington Post argues that the US government's AI strategy has a critical weakness: it isn't doing enough to control the supply of advanced AI chips (like those made by Nvidia) flowing to rivals like China. The argument is that while the US focuses on AI software policy, the hardware that powers AI — semiconductors — is still accessible in ways that undermine American AI dominance. This matters for investors in AI and semiconductor ETFs like GXAI.AX, as chip export controls could affect the whole sector.

stories.title: China's GLM-5.4 AI model launches — what it can actually do
stories.why_it_matters: China's Zhipu AI launched GLM-5.4, the latest in its series of large language models competing with ChatGPT and Gemini. The model is now available via API (meaning developers can build apps with it), with new pricing tiers. It's another sign that the US doesn't have a monopoly on frontier AI — Chinese models are closing the gap fast, which is relevant for the geopolitical AI competition that Penny Wong flagged as a foreign policy concern.

stories.title: Ant Group open-sources a medical AI model family
stories.why_it_matters: Alibaba-affiliate Ant Group has open-sourced its 'Afu' medical and health AI model family — meaning the code is freely available for hospitals, researchers, and developers to use and build on. This is significant because medical AI has historically been locked inside large tech companies. Open-sourcing it could accelerate healthcare AI adoption globally, including in Australia. It's also a competitive move by China to establish influence in a high-stakes AI domain.

sport.summary: Carlos Alcaraz made history at the ATP Finals, Jannik Sinner faces a lengthy injury lay-off, the NRL Grand Final delivered a thriller with the Roosters edging the Knights 19-18, and the AFL off-season is in full swing with draft and tribunal news.

stories.title: Roosters 19 def. Knights 18 — NRL Grand Final goes down to the wire
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters won the 2026 NRL Grand Final by the slimmest of margins, defeating the Newcastle Knights 19-18 at Accor Stadium on Sunday evening. One point in a Grand Final — it doesn't get more dramatic than that. A result that will be talked about for years on the Gold Coast and beyond.

stories.title: Alcaraz beats Zverev to win ATP Finals — joins Agassi, Federer, Djokovic in elite club
stories.why_it_matters: Carlos Alcaraz defeated Alexander Zverev to claim the ATP Finals title in Turin, completing a career set that only three other players have ever achieved — Agassi, Federer, and Djokovic (all winners of all four Grand Slams AND the ATP Finals). At 23 years old, Alcaraz is now firmly in the conversation as the greatest player of his generation and possibly all time. A historic moment for the sport.

stories.title: Jannik Sinner faces surgery — could miss Australian Open and Wimbledon 2027
stories.why_it_matters: World No. 1 Jannik Sinner is reportedly facing surgery and could be sidelined until Wimbledon — meaning he may miss both the Australian Open and Roland Garros in 2027. That's a massive blow for tennis fans heading into the Australian summer season. With Sinner out, the door swings wide open for Alcaraz (fresh off his ATP Finals win) and others to dominate early 2027.

stories.title: AFL Draft wrap: Essendon signs 209cm giant, former Roo gets lifeline
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL rookie draft is done, with Essendon signing a 209cm ruckman as the headline move. Nine players received rookie lifelines, including a former North Melbourne player getting another chance at the top level. Fox Sports also reported a major AFL Tribunal rule change is in the works that could affect how suspension decisions are made in 2027 — worth watching for footy fans.

stories.title: AFLW Rising Star: midfield trio the frontrunners for the award
stories.why_it_matters: Three midfielders are the frontrunners for the 2026 AFLW Rising Star award with the season wrapping up. The award recognises the best young player in the women's competition. No article text was available for specific names, but the AFLW season has been strong with high quality on display across the midfield this year.
